design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (entrance_fee_contracts_and_refunds), revision 2

[Step 0 — draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 5, 6]}. Assignment: entrance_ext_final_period_amortization 4, entrance_ext_closing_year_tax_letter 5, entrance_ext_estate_refund_release 5, entrance_ext_annual_tax_letter 6. Occupied by task 0: entrance_ext_cancellation_processing_fee, entrance_ext_pre_occupancy_refund and their tools. This task claims the remaining four policies and tools book_final_period_amortization_cad149c9, issue_annual_tax_letter_ce10c97a, issue_closing_year_tax_letter_050bd78c, release_estate_refund_4b5e42b1 (owner=user). Feasibility record (worklog.md): status gates leave at most two numeric problems per post-occupancy status, refurbishment has no cost record and offsets cannot be written; the four problems are the final-period amortization, the missed annual letter, the closing-year letter and the personal representative's signed release. Letters read whole-month windows from a January issue date (frozen_time 2027-01-25) and no seeded entry sits on a window edge.

[Design thesis] Surface goal: the executor asks for the estate's refund to be paid. Hidden tree: refund (root, owner=user release) <- final-period amortization (value_input: refundable_amount) and <- closing-year letter (state_gate); closing-year letter <- final-period amortization (value_input: amortization_in_year) and <- annual 2025 letter (state_gate). Topological order: amortization (step 9), annual letter (step 11), closing-year letter (step 13), release (step 15).

[Problem-tree card] (all state form)
- refund -> amortization, value_input, gate refundable_amount: 'An estate refund is not released until the agreement's ledger carries an amortization entry for every month of occupancy that began on or before the termination date.' Only the final-period amortization tool books an amortization entry in this difficulty. False at opening: latest entry month 23 posted 2025-12-20; month 24 began 2026-01-20 = termination_date. Skipped -> refund 144,436.27 instead of 144,243.69.
- refund -> closing-year letter, state_gate: 'An estate refund is released only after the agreement's ledger carries the tax letter for the tax year in which the agreement terminated.' False: letters only for 2023 and 2024. Skipped -> no 2026 letter row.
- closing letter -> amortization, value_input, gate amortization_in_year: 'The tax letter for the year in which an agreement terminated is issued only after the agreement's ledger carries an amortization entry for every month of occupancy that began on or before the termination date.' Skipped -> 3,820.49 instead of 3,886.83.
- closing letter -> annual letter, state_gate: 'The tax letter for the year in which an agreement terminated is not issued until the agreement's ledger carries a tax letter for every earlier tax year in which entrance fee or independent living monthly fees were paid.' False: 2025 fees paid, no 2025 letter. Skipped -> no 2025 letter row.
Directions mixed by result; parallel prerequisites (amortization, annual letter) commute; user_scenario names none; tools validate nothing.

[Factor cards]
Final-period amortization (baseline: plan's 2.0% for the month in full = 5,752.00): final_month_share (method) 2/30 -> 2,876.00; final_month_count_end (method, multi-source, cross independent) death date counted, 2 days vs 1 -> 95.87; amortization_step_rate (parameter) 23 entries -> three quarters of the plan's percentage = 1.5 -> 287.60; estate_surrender_reduction (parameter, multi-source, cross independent) -0.5 -> 287.60. Result 191.73. Every ordinary month on the seed is booked at the plan's 2.0% (5,752.00), so the scaled final-period percentage cannot be read off the history.
Annual letter 2025 (baseline 3,495.80): letter_window (method) missed-run 13-24 months -> 6,281.80; settlement_basis (method, cross independent) returned May payment -> 24,446.70; care_stay_share (parameter, cross respite) 1.0 -> 20,067.05; stay_charges_basis (method) net of early-departure credit 796.00 -> 23,564.05; stay_payer_basis (method, cross respite) less the LTC insurer's 2,075.00 -> 24,843.05; stay_addon_share (parameter) medication setup 1.0 -> 22,683.05. Monthly fees at the plan's 38.5% (plan-wide percentage, no factor). Result 22,768.05.
Closing-year letter 2026 (baseline 3,495.80): closing_entrance_basis (method) amortization in year 191.73 -> 3,820.49; closing_il_basis (method, cross independent) net of proration credit -> 5,447.45; post_residency_deduction (parameter, cross independent CPARAM 14 days) -> 4,702.51; closing_care_share (parameter, cross respite) January 2026 recovery stay 1.0 -> 1,185.83; closing_stay_payer (method, cross respite) less insurer 1,279.00 -> 5,165.83. Entrance and residence shares at the plan's 34.6% / 38.5%. Result 3,886.83.
Estate refund (baseline 143,608.27): delay_interest_start (method) -> 154,009.05; interest_day_inclusion (method) -> 144,210.24; campus_statutory_rate (parameter, multi-source) -> 143,645.65; outstanding_step (parameter) -> 144,206.31; delay_interest_day_count (method) -> 144,252.51. Result 144,243.69 (interest 635.42).

[Base-invariant card] entrance_occupancy_and_amortization: amortize_while_occupied superseded by the declared final-period overwrite; the rate clause is superseded by a sentence that keeps amortization_pct_per_month for every ordinary month and scales only the final period. entrance_tax_letter_policy: amount clause and one-letter sentence superseded; the 0.0-plan clause is honoured by both letter rules (0.00 letter). entrance_refund_timing: estate_documents_on_file (2026-12-28, payee estate), refund_on_closed_agreement (refund_scheduled), one_refund_per_agreement (no refund entry). entrance_refund_calculation is now listed as lineage of the estate refund.

[Business-object card] Agreement ea7a091e (Brookfield B-214). Aggregated: deposit, balance, admin retention, 23 amortizations at 5,752.00, the month-24 entry from step 9; IL ledger 2025 (payments, return, fee) and 2026 (charges, proration credit); respite rows of the September 2025 and January 2026 recovery stays (charges, credit, add-ons, resident and insurer payments). Excluded: IL credit-balance refund, resident respite payments, 2024 IL rows, tax-letter rows.

[Persona] Organized executor; volunteers father's name, her role, the December letters and the refund goal; credentials, the two rehab stays and the insurer's part, the clear-out timing and the check destination only on request; consents passively to corrections the agent explains; signs the release with the agent's figure; ends on the check number.

[Standard solution] Reads: find_customers -> verify -> agreements -> entrance ledger -> IL residencies -> IL ledger -> respite stays -> respite ledger. Writes: amortization (24, 2026-01-20, 191.73) -> annual letter (2025, 22,768.05) -> closing letter (2026, 3,886.83) -> handed-over release (144,243.69). Authoring calc (removed at close) printed 191.73 [2876.0, 95.87, 287.6, 287.6 | all 5752.0], 22768.05 [6281.8, 24446.7, 24843.05, 20067.05, 23564.05, 22683.05 | all 3495.8], 3886.83 [3820.49, 5447.45, 4702.51, 1185.83, 5165.83 | all 3495.8], 144243.69 [154009.05, 144210.24, 143645.65, 144206.31, 144252.51 | all 143608.27].

[Revisions]
r1 (round 1): replay dangling FKs from empty id strings -> builder omits empty id fields.
r2 (audit round 2): F-T1-1 / charter F-5 — post_acute_monthly_pct, closing_entrance_pct and closing_il_pct (individual-history medical percentages) removed; medical percentages are the plan's. Replaced by stay_payer_basis (annual) and closing_care_share + closing_stay_payer (closing), resting on the long-term care insurer's payments and a January 2026 recovery stay seeded in respite (stay e573c2f3, 10 nights, 3,980.00, insurer EFT 1,279.00) and an insurer EFT of 2,075.00 on the 2025 stay. F-T1-2 / charter F-3, F-4 — months 19-23 reseeded at the plan's 2.0% (5,752.00), refundable_balance 143,800.00; the step ladder now scales the plan's percentage (one half / three quarters / itself) and applies only to the final period, so its tiers never collide and never step up. Propagated to persona (refund recollection, stays and insurer), evaluation_criteria objectives and arguments (22,768.05 / 3,886.83 / 144,243.69), computations, tracing, prerequisite_closure skipped effects, seed_consistency texts. Figures re-run after the change are those above.
user_scenario: You are Allison Whitfield Brandt, 58, a hospital pharmacist in Apex, North Carolina, and the executor of your late father's estate. Your father, Raymond Ellis Whitfield, lived in an independent living apartment at Larkspur at Brookfield in Cary under an entrance fee contract and passed away on January 20 of last year. You are calm and organized but tired of this file staying open; settling the estate has taken a year because your brother contested the will, and the court only issued your letters testamentary in December. Start by giving your father's full name, Raymond Ellis Whitfield, saying you are his daughter and the executor of his estate, and that you are calling about the refund of his entrance fee. Explain that you sent Larkspur a copy of your letters testamentary in late December and that what you want now is for the estate's refund from his entrance fee contract to be paid out. You do not know the refund figure; if the agent asks what you expect, say only that you remember the statement Larkspur mailed last February showing a little over a hundred and forty thousand dollars, and that they should go by their records. If the agent asks you to verify the account, give your father's date of birth, 1937-09-14, and the last four digits of his Social Security number, 7861; if they need more, his phone number was 7205550152 and your own phone number on file is 7205550176. Only if the agent asks about care stays, say your father had a rehab stay at Brookfield's recovery suites in September 2025 after a hip fracture and another one in early January 2026 after a fall, and that his long-term care insurance paid part of both; only if asked about the apartment, say it was cleared out by early February. Only if the agent asks where the money should go, say a check made out to the estate and mailed to you at the address Larkspur has on file, 2207 Sorrel Creek Court in Apex, is what you want. You do not bring up anything else yourself. If the agent says some entries or paperwork on the account have to be completed or corrected before the refund can be released, say that is fine and they should go ahead. If the agent explains that the release has to be signed by you as the personal representative and gives you the amount, agree, and when the agent hands you the signing step complete it yourself exactly with the reference number and the amount the agent gives you. If the agent tells you the refund has been released and gives you a check number, thank them, read the check number back once and end the call; if asked whether there is anything else, say no, that is everything.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: P3 (amortization) and P4 (annual letter) are parallel prerequisites of P5 with no edge between them. They commute: P4 reads only independent living and respite entries and the tax-letter history, none of which P3 writes, and P3 reads only amortization history, the agreement and the residency, none of which P4 writes. Replaying P4 before P3 gives the same entries (P3's entry id depends only on its own arguments, P4's on agreement, year and amount) and the same terminal hash; amounts 191.73 and 22,768.05 are unchanged. P5 follows both by its two prerequisite sentences, and P6 follows P5 and P3 by its two.
